topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces herself, the cancer lecture series, and the core learning outcomes concerning cancer causes, carcinogenicity testing, and initiation versus promotion.

topics.label: The Nature of Cancer and Sources of Genetic Mutation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics define cancer as an evolutionary genetic disease shaped by the microenvironment and outline how endogenous metabolic stress, environmental insults, and inherited predispositions contribute to mutation acquisition.

topics.label: Environmental Exposures and Epidemiological Evidence
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore diverse environmental carcinogens and evaluate epidemiological and migrant data to assess the relative roles of environmental exposure, genetics, and random chance in cancer risk.

topics.label: Infectious Pathogens and Burkitt Lymphoma
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss how infectious agents contribute to oncogenesis, using Denis Burkitt's discovery and the interplay of malaria and Epstein-Barr virus in Burkitt lymphoma as a primary case study.

topics.label: Mechanisms of Direct and Metabolically Activated Mutagens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the molecular mechanisms by which chemical and physical mutagens—including dietary aflatoxin, UV radiation, polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons, TCDD, and beta-naphthylamine—induce DNA damage and bulky adducts.

topics.label: Tumor Promotion and the Multi-Stage Model of Carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how non-mutagenic promoters drive cancer through chronic inflammation and intracellular signaling, detailing asbestos pathology and the Berenbaum initiator-promoter model.

topics.label: Host Developmental Susceptibility and Carcinogenesis Summary
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how developmental timing and life stage alter tissue susceptibility to carcinogens and summarise the foundational principles of mutagenic and promotional mechanisms in cancer development.

topics.label: Methodologies for Identifying and Testing Carcinogens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics review the scientific methodologies used to establish carcinogenicity, including mutational signature sequencing, biobank epidemiology, in vivo animal toxicology studies, and the in vitro Ames test.

topics.label: Risk-Benefit Decision-Making and Lecture Conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the lecture by reflecting on personal risk-benefit evaluations regarding exposure to carcinogens and summarizing the main takeaways of the session.
